name: Radxa ROCK 5 ITX
summary: An ARM desktop, from boot to accelerated graphics.
features: NVMe boot, multicore CPU and onboard Ethernet
Mali GPU acceleration with Mesa Panfrost
Rockchip MPP video decoding and analog audio
Intel AX210 Wi-Fi, including tested 802.11ax association
limits: Wi-Fi 6 mode coverage and Bluetooth pairing remain incomplete. Results are specific to the ROCK 5 ITX lab board.

image.alt: Radxa ROCK 5 ITX motherboard viewed from above

name: Radxa Cubie A7S
summary: A compact ARM desktop with PowerVR graphics and onboard wireless.
features: Bootable SD image and native Haiku desktop
PowerVR BXM-4-64 graphics through Mesa Zink: OpenGL 3.2 and OpenGL ES 3.1
Summit WebGL 1 and 2, with transform feedback support
Onboard AIC8800 Wi-Fi: 5 GHz WPA2, 802.11ac, DHCP and reconnection
Bluetooth Low Energy discovery; an A2DP audio implementation is available for testing
limits: Bluetooth speaker pairing and audio over the air remain unverified on this board. Cooling matters under sustained load. The Cubie SD image is its own download; the generic ARM64 ISO does not boot this board.

image.alt: Radxa Cubie A7S board shown from the front, back and side

name: Radxa Dragon Q8B
summary: A Snapdragon desktop board, booting airOS through its UEFI firmware.
features: UEFI boot with the firmware’s display resolution and on-screen kernel output
All eight Kryo CPU cores, from the device tree
Native PCIe host driver and GICv3 ITS: NVMe on MSI-X, reading at 795 MB/s
USB 3 through the Qualcomm DWC3 controllers
Kernel serial console on the GENI debug UART
limits: Adreno graphics, video decoding, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and audio are not yet working, and there is no public image. This work lives on the dragon-q8b branch until it is merged.

image.alt: Radxa Dragon Q8B board shown from the front, side and back

name: Raspberry Pi 4
summary: A bootable SD image for the small, familiar computer.
features: SD-card first-run setup: expand the filesystem, set the timezone and synchronize the clock
Dual HDMI desktop with display arrangement and tested disconnect/reconnect recovery
V3D accelerated OpenGL and WebGL, with lower-copy EGL window presentation
Hardware H.264 and HEVC decoding, Ethernet and onboard Wi-Fi
Waveshare 3.5-inch DSI auxiliary display with AirTop CPU, network and temperature panels
limits: DSI touch and Bluetooth pairing are not verified. HDMI audio output has not been listened to. Video throughput depends on codec, resolution and presentation path; see the media tests.

name: AMD Radeon Pro WX 5100
summary: An accelerated desktop on AMD: native display output, graphics and video.
features: Linux 6.18 amdgpu driver port with DRM, memory management and Display Core integrated into Haiku
Two 3840 × 2160 displays at 60 Hz, with scaling, arrangement and tested DisplayPort hotplug
Mesa radeonsi for OpenGL, OpenGL ES and Summit GPU compositing
RADV Vulkan 1.4, including windowed Vulkan through the in-process Wayland server
UVD H.264, HEVC and Main 10 decoding; VCE H.264/HEVC encoding
airTime 4K H.264 at 60 fps and HEVC Main 10 at 30 fps without drops in the recorded trials
limits: These results apply to the tested WX 5100, not every AMD GPU. Mixed-scale layouts can use a software cursor. Sustained mixed video/Vulkan stress has exposed rare decode mismatches; the detailed record describes fixes and remaining limits.

links.label: Workstation support and earlier NVIDIA tests

name: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 / GTX 1080 Ti
summary: Native NVIDIA graphics and hardware video decoding, with an experimental encoding path.
features: Native display output through nvidia_rm, with dual 4K monitors, per-display scaling and desktop arrangement
Mesa NVK Vulkan and Zink OpenGL 4.5 on the tested Pascal cards
NVDEC hardware H.264 decoding through a system media add-on: tested GTX 1080 Ti streams match FFmpeg software decoding byte for byte
NVDEC decoded the recorded 1080p test at 232 frames per second; NVPlay provides playback with audio and seeking
Experimental NVENC integration in MediaConverter for H.264, HEVC Main and HEVC Main 10 on compatible encoder generations
NVENC must pass an encode/decode self-test for each card and format before use; failed or unavailable encoding paths use the CPU
limits: NVENC has not yet been validated on an NVIDIA card; its application integration was tested with a software stand-in. B-frame encoding is not implemented, and AV1 encoding uses the CPU, including on Ada and Blackwell. Verified NVDEC coverage is progressive 8-bit 4:2:0 H.264; interlaced, 4:2:2 and higher-bit-depth streams are unsupported and may fail to play instead of falling back. NVIDIA 2D drawing remains unaccelerated. These results describe the earlier Pascal workstation configuration, not every NVIDIA GPU.

name: Framework Laptop 13
summary: AMD graphics on a high-density laptop desktop.
features: Native desktop output through amdgpu_drm
Scaled desktop and native application windows; the Craft ports have been checked at 175% density
MediaConverter detects the Radeon 760M and offers hardware H.264 encoding
limits: This is the tested Radeon 760M configuration, not a claim about every Framework model. Suspend and resume remain development work. See the driver source and current package notes for device-specific coverage.
